hlni.insight: Preference for a topic does not equal institutional requirement or degree fit.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume liking a subject makes it the 'correct' degree choice.
hlni.viewerChange: Viewers transition from emotional guessing to checking specific course requirements.
hlni.support: Distinguishes desire from confirmation; prioritizes verification over assumption.
hlni.payoff: The viewer now knows to ask if their interest is a core requirement or elective.

creativeAngle: Distinguishing personal preference from operational requirement
objective: Help students evaluate B.Com and BBA by separating interest from degree structure
targetAudience: +2 students seeking accessible, supportive guidance, including students worried about marks, confidence, or belonging

shots.name: The Preference Dilemma
shots.visual: A student sits at a desk with two cards labelled B.Com and BBA. They look unsure.
shots.dialogue: Choosing between B.Com and BBA feels like picking a personality. But liking a topic isn't the same as course fit.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on student, then the cards.

shots.name: The Method Display
shots.visual: A screen showing a checklist app interface.
shots.dialogue: Try this check. List your interest, then see if it's actually required or just an elective.
shots.onscreenText: Example: My interest: Leadership. Required prerequisite: ? Status: Pending verification.

shots.name: The Next Action
shots.visual: Student looks at the camera, nodding confidently.
shots.dialogue: Ask yourself: Is this interest a required subject or an elective I can choose? Verify that first.
shots.onscreenText: Is this interest a required subject or an elective I can choose?

productionNotes.camera: Stable tripod shots with clear focus on visual inputs.
productionNotes.editing: Rhythmic cuts matching the checklist progression.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Use a verification method to separate personal preference from structural requirements.

selected.title: The Preference Check
selected.audienceGap: Students assume that because they like a topic, it is the 'right' degree for them.
selected.hlni: An appealing option and an available option are different questions. Unknown requirements should be recorded as checks rather than assumed to be satisfied.
selected.viewerChange: Viewers learn to separate their preference from the operational requirements.
selected.concept: A student lists their favorite topics and matches them against unknown requirements.
selected.device: A checklist app interface where 'wishlist' items are marked as 'need to verify'.
selected.support: The method distinguishes a desire from confirmation; it asserts no particular institutional rule.
methodSteps: List the actual requirements you need to check and mark unknowns.
Verify an unknown before treating the option as available.
selected.interpretationRule: Use an unknown requirement as the next verification task; preference alone is not confirmation.
selected.visibleProof: A preference card moves to a provisional list until one concrete requirement is checked.
selected.payoff: Use an unknown requirement as the next verification task; preference alone is not confirmation.
selected.limitations: Never invent eligibility rules, admission availability or prerequisites.

demonstration.input: A list of student interests (e.g., leadership, finance) vs course requirements.
demonstration.visibleInput: Example: My interest: Leadership. Required prerequisite: ? Status: Pending verification.
demonstration.observation: Preference for a topic does not equate to confirmed enrollment or fit.
demonstration.nextQuestion: Is this interest a required subject or an elective I can choose?

comparedWith.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
